text: Current research has studied numerous variables regarding virtual assistants and how they are perceived.It was discovered by Osmers et al. [11] that human representations seem to have a positive impact on thesocial presence of a virtual assistant. Guo et al. [5] studied the effects of assistants having a similar voiceand appearance to the participant, concluding a higher co-presence and perceived intelligence but also moreeeriness with a self similar appearance. Studying the effect of appearance on robots, Strathearn and Ma [13]concluded that younger participants preferred younger looking robots for interaction and more senior onesolder looking versions. According to the results of Nam et al. [10], perceived usefulness and satisfaction andacceptance of virtual assistants is enhanced with providing expression. It was explicitly stated that genderimplications were not part of the experiment.
